title: Building of the Ka'bah by Ibrahim and Isma'il عليهما السلام
commentary: Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) and his son Isma'il (Ishmael) built the Ka'bah in Makkah as the first house of worship dedicated to the One God.

title: Prophet Musa (Moses) عليه السلام
commentary: Prophet Musa received the Torah and led the Children of Israel out of Egypt. He is one of the greatest prophets and is mentioned frequently in the Quran.

title: Prophet 'Isa (Jesus) عليه السلام
commentary: Prophet 'Isa was born to Maryam (Mary) by a miracle. He performed miracles and preached the message of monotheism. He foretold the coming of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
notes: Born approximately 4 BCE, mentioned in Quran as giving glad tidings of Ahmad

title: Birth of 'Abdul-Muttalib
commentary: Grandfather of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. He was the chief of Quraysh and rediscovered the well of Zamzam.

title: Rediscovery of Zamzam Well
commentary: 'Abdul-Muttalib rediscovered the well of Zamzam in Makkah, which had been buried for centuries. This well was originally created by Allah for Hajar and Isma'il.
notes: Miracle well that still flows today

title: Birth of 'Abdullah (Father of the Prophet ﷺ)
commentary: 'Abdullah ibn 'Abdul-Muttalib was born. He was known for his exceptional beauty and piety. He would become the father of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

title: The Year of the Elephant
commentary: Abraha, the Abyssinian ruler of Yemen, led an army with elephants to destroy the Ka'bah. Allah sent flocks of birds (Ababil) carrying stones to destroy the army. This event is mentioned in Surah Al-Fil.
notes: The year of the Prophet's birth

title: Death of 'Abdullah (Father of the Prophet ﷺ)
commentary: 'Abdullah passed away before the birth of his son Muhammad ﷺ. He died while returning from a trade journey to Syria, leaving Aminah pregnant.
notes: The Prophet ﷺ was born an orphan

title: Birth of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
commentary: He was named by his grandfather 'Abdul-Muttalib. Born in Makkah in the Year of the Elephant.

title: Death of his mother Aminah
commentary: The Prophet's mother, Aminah, passed away from severe illness in Abwa on the road between Makkah and Madinah

title: Death of his grandfather 'Abdul-Muttalib
commentary: 'Abdul-Muttalib, the grandfather of the Prophet ﷺ, passed away. His uncle Abu Talib took care of him.

title: Journey to Syria with Abu Talib
commentary: The Prophet ﷺ traveled with his uncle Abu Talib to Syria for trade. The monk Bahira recognized signs of prophethood in him.

title: Participated in Hilf al-Fudul
commentary: The Prophet ﷺ participated in the Hilf al-Fudul (Alliance of the Virtuous), a pact to help the oppressed in Makkah.

title: Marriage to Khadijah رضي الله عنها
commentary: The Prophet ﷺ married Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, a noble and wealthy woman of Makkah. She was 40 and he was 25.

title: Rebuilding of the Ka'bah
commentary: The Quraysh rebuilt the Ka'bah. The Prophet ﷺ resolved a dispute about who would place the Black Stone by having all tribes lift it together.

title: First Revelation
commentary: Angel Jibril appeared to the Prophet ﷺ in the cave of Hira and revealed the first verses of the Quran: 'Read in the name of your Lord...' (Surah Al-'Alaq)

title: Beginning of Secret Da'wah
commentary: The Prophet ﷺ began calling people to Islam secretly. The first to accept Islam were Khadijah, Ali, Zayd ibn Harithah, and Abu Bakr.

title: Public Preaching Begins
commentary: Allah commanded the Prophet ﷺ to preach openly. He climbed Mount Safa and called the Quraysh to Islam publicly.

title: First Migration to Abyssinia
commentary: Due to severe persecution, the Prophet ﷺ advised some Muslims to migrate to Abyssinia (Ethiopia) where the Christian king was just.

title: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab accepts Islam
commentary: 'Umar رضي الله عنه accepted Islam, strengthening the Muslim community. The Muslims were able to pray openly at the Ka'bah.

title: Year of Sorrow
commentary: Both Khadijah رضي الله عنها and Abu Talib passed away in the same year, leaving the Prophet ﷺ without his greatest supporter and protector.

title: Journey to Ta'if
commentary: The Prophet ﷺ traveled to Ta'if seeking support, but was rejected and stoned. Angel Jibril offered to destroy the city, but the Prophet ﷺ refused and prayed for their guidance.

title: Al-Isra' wal-Mi'raj (Night Journey)
commentary: The Prophet ﷺ was taken from Makkah to Jerusalem (Isra') and then ascended to the heavens (Mi'raj), where he met the prophets and received the command of five daily prayers.

title: First Pledge of 'Aqabah
commentary: Six men from Yathrib (Madinah) met the Prophet ﷺ and accepted Islam, pledging to support him.

title: Second Pledge of 'Aqabah
commentary: 73 men and 2 women from Madinah pledged to protect the Prophet ﷺ as they would their own families, paving the way for Hijrah.

title: Hijrah to Madinah
commentary: The Prophet ﷺ migrated from Makkah to Madinah, escaping assassination. This marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar.

title: Building of Masjid an-Nabawi
commentary: The Prophet ﷺ built the first mosque in Madinah, which became the center of the Muslim community.

title: Brotherhood between Muhajirun and Ansar
commentary: The Prophet ﷺ established brotherhood between the Migrants (Muhajirun) and the Helpers (Ansar) of Madinah.

title: Battle of Badr
commentary: The first major battle between Muslims (313) and Quraysh (1000). Allah granted victory to the Muslims despite being outnumbered.

title: Battle of Uhud
commentary: The Quraysh returned with 3000 warriors. The Muslims initially won but suffered losses when archers left their positions. The Prophet ﷺ was injured.

title: Battle of the Trench (Khandaq)
commentary: The Quraysh and their allies besieged Madinah with 10,000 warriors. The Muslims dug a trench on Salman al-Farsi's advice and successfully defended the city.

title: Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
commentary: The Prophet ﷺ and the Quraysh signed a peace treaty. Though it seemed unfavorable, it was called a 'clear victory' in the Quran and led to many conversions.

title: Letters to Kings and Rulers
commentary: The Prophet ﷺ sent letters inviting world leaders to Islam, including the Byzantine Emperor, Persian King, and Egyptian ruler.

title: Conquest of Khaybar
commentary: The Muslims conquered the Jewish fortress of Khaybar. The Prophet ﷺ married Safiyyah رضي الله عنها.

title: Battle of Mu'tah
commentary: 3000 Muslims faced 200,000 Byzantine and Arab forces. Zayd, Ja'far, and Abdullah ibn Rawahah were martyred. Khalid ibn al-Walid led a tactical retreat.

title: Conquest of Makkah
commentary: The Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah peacefully with 10,000 Muslims. He forgave his enemies and purified the Ka'bah of idols.

title: Battle of Hunayn
commentary: Shortly after Makkah's conquest, the Muslims faced the Hawazin tribe. After initial setback, they achieved victory.

title: Battle of Tabuk
commentary: The Prophet ﷺ led 30,000 Muslims to Tabuk to face the Byzantine threat. The Byzantines did not show up, and many tribes pledged allegiance to Islam.

title: Year of Delegations
commentary: Tribes from all over Arabia sent delegations to Madinah to accept Islam. Islam spread rapidly throughout the peninsula.

title: Farewell Pilgrimage
commentary: The Prophet ﷺ performed his first and last Hajj with over 100,000 Muslims. He delivered the Farewell Sermon establishing human rights and equality.

title: Revelation of Final Verse
commentary: During the Farewell Pilgrimage, the verse was revealed: 'This day I have perfected your religion for you...' (Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:3)

title: Death of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
commentary: The Prophet ﷺ passed away in Madinah in the house of 'Aishah رضي الله عنها, at the age of 63. He was buried in the same place.

title: Death of Abu Bakr as-Siddiq رضي الله عنه
commentary: The first Caliph and closest companion of the Prophet ﷺ passed away. He was one of the greatest narrators of hadith and the first man to accept Islam.

title: Death of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab رضي الله عنه
commentary: The second Caliph, known for his justice and strength. He was assassinated while leading Fajr prayer. Major narrator of hadith.

title: Death of 'Uthman ibn 'Affan رضي الله عنه
commentary: The third Caliph, who compiled the Quran into one standard text. He was martyred during a siege of his house.

title: Death of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib رضي الله عنه
commentary: The fourth Caliph, cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet ﷺ. He was one of the first to accept Islam and a great scholar.

title: Death of 'Aishah رضي الله عنها
commentary: Wife of the Prophet ﷺ and one of the greatest scholars of Islam. She was the most knowledgeable woman in hadith and Islamic jurisprudence.
notes: Narrated 2,210 hadiths - one of the top narrators

title: Death of Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه
commentary: The greatest narrator of hadith, who memorized and transmitted more hadiths than any other companion. He dedicated his life to learning from the Prophet ﷺ.
notes: Narrated 5,374 hadiths - the most prolific narrator

title: Death of Abdullah ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنه
commentary: Son of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, known for his piety and strict adherence to the Sunnah. Major narrator of hadith.

title: Death of Anas ibn Malik رضي الله عنه
commentary: Personal servant of the Prophet ﷺ for 10 years. He was the last companion to die in Basra and narrated many hadiths.

title: Birth of Imam Malik ibn Anas
commentary: The great Imam of Madinah, founder of the Maliki school of jurisprudence. He compiled Al-Muwatta, one of the earliest hadith collections.

title: Death of Imam Malik ibn Anas
commentary: Imam Malik passed away in Madinah after a lifetime of teaching and preserving the Sunnah. His Muwatta contains 1,720 hadiths.

title: Birth of Imam Abu Dawud
commentary: Compiler of Sunan Abu Dawud, one of the six major hadith collections (Kutub al-Sittah). His collection focuses on legal hadiths.
notes: Author of Sunan Abu Dawud (4,800 hadiths)

title: Birth of Imam al-Bukhari
commentary: The greatest hadith scholar, compiler of Sahih al-Bukhari, the most authentic book after the Quran. He memorized 600,000 hadiths.
notes: Author of Sahih al-Bukhari (7,563 hadiths with repetitions)

title: Birth of Imam Muslim
commentary: Compiler of Sahih Muslim, the second most authentic hadith collection. He traveled extensively to collect hadiths from scholars.
notes: Author of Sahih Muslim (12,000 hadiths with repetitions)

title: Birth of Imam al-Tirmidhi
commentary: Compiler of Jami' at-Tirmidhi, one of the six major hadith collections. Known for his critical analysis of hadith authenticity.

title: Birth of Imam al-Nasa'i
commentary: Compiler of Sunan an-Nasa'i, one of the six major hadith collections. Known for his strict criteria in hadith authentication.

title: Birth of Imam Ibn Majah
commentary: Compiler of Sunan Ibn Majah, the sixth of the major hadith collections. He was a scholar of hadith and Quranic exegesis.
notes: Author of Sunan Ibn Majah (4,341 hadiths)

title: Death of Imam al-Bukhari
commentary: Imam al-Bukhari passed away after dedicating his life to preserving authentic hadiths. His Sahih is considered the most authentic book after the Quran.

title: Death of Imam Muslim
commentary: Imam Muslim passed away in Nishapur. His Sahih Muslim is the second most authentic hadith collection.

title: Death of Imam Abu Dawud
commentary: Imam Abu Dawud passed away in Basra. His Sunan is essential for Islamic jurisprudence.

title: Death of Imam Ibn Majah
commentary: Imam Ibn Majah passed away in Qazvin. His Sunan completes the six major hadith collections.

title: Death of Imam al-Tirmidhi
commentary: Imam al-Tirmidhi passed away in Tirmidh. His Jami' is known for its detailed commentary on hadith grades.

title: Death of Imam al-Nasa'i
commentary: Imam al-Nasa'i was martyred in Damascus after being beaten for his support of 'Ali رضي الله عنه. His Sunan is highly regarded for its authenticity.
